podcast.title: Encounter with Kurt Cobain (April 1, 1994)
podcast.body: Duff McKagan, the bassist for Guns N' Roses, coincidentally sat next to Kurt Cobain in business class on Delta Flight 788 as Cobain flew back to Seattle from Los Angeles. McKagan reported that Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride home from the airport, but Kurt declined, signed an autograph for two people, and then disappeared. "By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses' bass player, Duff McCagan. Duff says the Kurt seemed fine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Intervention for Scott Weiland (2003)
podcast.body: When Scott Weiland struggled with addiction during the recording of Velvet Revolver's debut album, Duff McKagan personally took him to a rural retreat in Washington state. There, Weiland underwent intense physical training with a martial arts expert to help him overcome his issues. "Duff took him to a quiet rural place in Washington state to commune with his trainer, a martial arts expert who promised that Scott would work out his issues with him intense physical training."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Velvet Revolver Formation (2003)
podcast.body: After reconciling with Slash and Matt Sorum, Duff McKagan was one of the three core Guns N' Roses members who initiated the formation of Velvet Revolver, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cool and Friendly Demeanor (2004)
podcast.body: At a press conference for Velvet Revolver's "Contraband" album, Duff McKagan, along with Slash and Matt Sorum, were observed as "cool, all very friendly, all hanging out together," in stark contrast to Scott Weiland's aloofness. "The three guns and roses guys were cool, all very friendly, all hanging out together."

xref.title: 1992 MTV Music Video Awards Altercation
xref.body: The animosity between Nirvana and Guns N' Roses culminated in a backstage altercation at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards. Axl Rose confronted Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love, reportedly telling Kurt to "keep his woman in line." Simultaneously, Nirvana bassist Chris Novoselic and Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan were also arguing. "This boiled over to an altercation backstage at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards between Axel, Kurt and Courtney Love."

xref.title: Duff McKagan Pancreas Explosion (1994) – Near-Fatal Alcohol and Cocaine Abuse
xref.body: Bassist Duff McKagan suffered what was described as a "explosion" of his pancreas in 1994 as a result of severe alcohol and cocaine abuse, causing third-degree internal burns and nearly killing him. The incident led to his complete sobriety, which he has maintained ever since. "Experienced an 'explosion' of his pancreas due to alcohol and cocaine abuse, causing third-degree internal burns and nearly killing him."

xref.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan and Death (1994)
xref.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took Delta Flight 788 to Seattle and coincidentally sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan, also a veteran of rehab. Cobain refused a ride from McKagan upon landing, signed autographs, and disappeared. He then acquired drugs, returned to the room above the greenhouse at his and Courtney Love's Lake Washington Boulevard home, got high, and died by suicide, believed to be on April 5th, 1994. The news of his death broke on Friday, April 8th. "Soon, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, and by sheer coincidence, he was sitting next to Guns & Roses bass player Duff McAgan, himself, a junkie we have veteran."

xref.title: Return to Seattle and Final Days (1994)
xref.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. Coincidentally, he sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan in business class, who later reported Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride, which Kurt declined. He signed an autograph and then disappeared. He made it back to his house before 2 AM on Saturday, April 2nd, and was last seen by the Cobains' former nanny, Callie, and her girlfriend around 6 AM that morning. "He took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses bass player Duff McKagan."

xref.title: Duff McKagan's Intervention and Martial Arts Training (2003)
xref.body: After an initial rehab stint for Velvet Revolver's debut album didn't work, Duff McKagan took Scott Weiland to a rural retreat in Washington state. There, a martial arts expert's intense physical training regimen helped Weiland get "straight and healthy again," leading him to find his own trainer in LA. xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

xref.body: Prior to recording their debut album, Scott Weiland underwent another trip to rehab to get straight. xref.title: Velvet Revolver Audition and Trust (2003)
xref.body: Scott Weiland initially disliked the music sent by the future Velvet Revolver members but agreed to jam after hearing a second, improved CD. Despite arriving hours late due to drug use, he found the chemistry with Duff McKagan, Slash, Matt Sorum, and Dave Kushner to be "bang on" and trusted Matt Sorum from a shared rehab experience. "Besides, he'd been in rehab with Matt Sorom so he trusted him."

xref.title: Ian Thorneley's Audition Experience
xref.body: Ian Thorneley rehearsed with Velvet Revolver in Los Angeles after Scott Weiland's departure. He found the musical aspect and chemistry to be strong, and the band members (Slash, Duff McKagan, etc.) to be "real dudes" and normal guys, contrary to any "reality show" perception. "It was really nice to see that. It wasn't, it wasn't the reality show, whatever that I had imagined it would be like."

xref.title: Reconciliation with Duff McKagan Before Death
xref.body: Days before Kurt Cobain's death, after leaving a rehab center in Los Angeles, he encountered Duff McKagan of Guns N' Roses on a Delta flight back to Seattle. They had a pleasant conversation, and Duff even offered Kurt a ride home from the airport, though Kurt vanished before taking it. "After walking away from a rehab center in Los Angeles, Kurt found himself on a Delta flight back to Seattle, sitting right next to Duff McKagan in business class."
